title: Winter Storm Recap: Jan. 14, 2022 (Worst Drivers)
description: MN Safety is made up of volunteers promoting traffic safety & 1st Responders. Not an official source. Videos + Education + Data = We all can be a little safer.

transcript.text: What do you do when it's snowy and icy and you have a wrong way driver coming at you on the freeway? This is Minnesota Highway 100. The vehicle is in the southbound lanes, traveling northbound, west metro side of the Twin Cities. And yes, they are driving with their hood up, possibly from a previous collision. Multiple vehicles you see on the left side of your screen, there's already one vehicle that slid off. Lots, very slippery area, lots of vehicles sliding around, and working hard to recover. And right as it passed, another look of a vehicle slipping and sliding in that same location. Now, going back to the wrong way driver, continued northbound, about a half mile longer, ended up being involved in a multi-vehicle collision, an ambulance was requested to the scene and a large police presence. State troopers can't catch a break this winter with all the stormy weather. vehicle was headed right for that trooper on the side before they corrected and struck another vehicle. While one vehicle even hit the pole for the traffic camera, State Patrol reports 377 crashes today, 214 vehicle spin-outs or off-road vehicles, four jack-knife semis, and that's just from 5 a.m. to 5 p.m. We'll do a full storm recap in less than 90 seconds. See if you can find the car that hit the traffic camera, the pickup that lost control with its trailer. the cargo van with the loose door, the car that tried to pass on the right, one car that had to make their exit no matter what, a truck that almost went off the bridge, and one crash that felt like it was happening in slow motion. Some crash scenes had backups over 30 minutes during the evening commute. Most of the northeast metro got an inch or two of snow while up to five inches fell in the southwest area of the Twin Cities, and the airport reported 3.7 inches. Areas north of Duluth, reported up to six inches of snow due to the lake effect. MN. Crime on Twitter also reported a snowmobile crash in Albany, Minnesota, with a Lifeline helicopter being requested. Now take a look as concrete walls, guardrails, like this one, and median cable barriers helped keep vehicles more or less on the road and clearly prevented them from going into oncoming traffic or existing crash scenes where they would have created an even bigger mess. this is your january 14 2020 storm recap please like subscribe help us bring this content out there help us keep producing it and of course be careful out there be minnesota safe
